mainTopic: Selling and repurposing a בית כנסת, disposing of holy objects, and ranking levels of קדושה
overview: This amud first finishes the topic of selling a בית כנסת. After a proper sale by the שבעה טובי העיר במעמד אנשי העיר, even the money from the sale may be spent on beer. רב אשי tells רבינא to buy the land of a ruined shul this way before planting it. רב פפא and רב הונא forbid רמי בר אבא to tear down an old shul before the new one is built, even though he planned to use its materials for the new one. רבא then rules that a shul may be sold or exchanged but not rented or mortgaged, and the same applies to its old bricks. רב אחא and רבינא disagree about giving a shul as a gift. Next, a ברייתא separates תשמישי מצוה, which may be thrown out, from תשמישי קדושה, which need גניזה. רבא applies this split to the reading stand, the ark curtain, broken arks, worn curtains and storage cases, and he fails to find a way for כהנים to pray in a shul next to a room with a dead body. The amud ends with rules for burying worn-out wrappings and ספרי תורה, and two opposite versions of רבא on turning a בית כנסת into a בית מדרש. A statement of רב אחא on this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even drinking beer with the sale money is fine
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the ruling from the end of the previous daf. When the שבעה טובי העיר sell a בית כנסת in front of the townspeople, the money has no holiness left. It may be used even for beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: To drink beer with it (the money from the sale) is perfectly fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence that began earlier: after a proper sale by the town's leaders, the money may be used for anything at all, even beer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beer is the most ordinary, everyday use one could think of. Allowing it shows that a proper sale by the שבעה טובי העיר במעמד אנשי העיר fully removes the קדושה. Nothing carries over to the money.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a ruling that started on the previous daf. The 'it' (בֵּיהּ) means the money from a properly done sale, not the shul building itself.

phrases.english: to drink beer with it (the proceeds)
phrases.notes: This continues the word 'even' from the previous daf: even this ordinary use is allowed.

phrases.english: is perfectly fine.
phrases.notes: The proper sale removed all holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ruling about a sale by the שבעה טובי העיר, which began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A sale by the שבעה טובי העיר במעמד אנשי העיר removes all קדושה, so the money may be used for anything.

steps.title: רבינא asks about planting on the land of a ruined shul
steps.stepSummary: רבינא owned a plot of land that held the ruins of a בית כנסת. He asked רב אשי whether he may plant crops there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא had a certain mound (of ruins) of a synagogue. He came before רב אשי and said to him: What is the law about sowing it?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבינא asks רב אשי whether he may plant crops on the land where a ruined shul once stood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shul has collapsed, but its ruins may still be holy. Planting would turn holy ground into an ordinary farm. The question is whether a ruin still holds קדושה that blocks this use.

phrases.english: Ravina had
phrases.notes: A story about רבינא begins.

phrases.english: a certain mound (of ruins) of a synagogue.
phrases.notes: The shul had collapsed into a pile of ruins.

phrases.english: He came before Rav Ashi,
phrases.notes: He went to his teacher to ask.

phrases.english: he said to him: What is the law about sowing it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the sale rule to a real case: a ruined shul.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May one plant crops on the land of a ruined בית כנסת?

steps.title: רב אשי: buy it properly first, then plant
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי tells רבינא to buy the land from the שבעה טובי העיר in front of the townspeople. After that he may plant it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go buy it from the seven leaders of the town in the presence of the townspeople, and then sow it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers. Planting is allowed, but only after a proper purchase that removes the holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruin still holds קדושה. Simply collapsing does not remove it. The way to remove it is the same official sale described in step 1. Once that sale is done, the land is ordinary and may be farmed.

keyTerms.meaning: the seven leaders/representatives of the town
in the presence of the townspeople

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruined shul is still holy. Its holiness ends only through the proper community sale.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go buy it
phrases.notes: רב אשי's instruction.

phrases.english: from the seven leaders of the town
phrases.notes: The community's official representatives.

phrases.english: in the presence of the townspeople, and then sow it.
phrases.notes: After the proper sale, planting is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ זִיל זַבְנֵיהּ מִשִּׁבְעָה טוֹבֵי הָעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Buy it through the שבעה טובי העיר במעמד אנשי העיר, then plant it.

steps.title: רמי בר אבא wants to reuse an old shul's materials
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא was building a new בית כנסת. He wanted to tear down an old one and move its bricks and beams to the new building.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא was building a synagogue. There was a certain old synagogue; he wanted to demolish it, bring bricks and beams from it, and bring them over there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story starts. The גמרא is setting up the case that leads to רמי בר אבא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not the case of an abandoned shul. The old shul still stands, and its materials would go straight into a new shul. These details set up the doubt that follows.

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא הֲוָה קָא בָנֵי בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא.
phrases.english: Rami bar Abba was building a synagogue.
There was a certain old synagogue,
phrases.notes: Still standing.

phrases.english: he wanted to demolish it
and bring bricks and beams from it
phrases.notes: Reusing the building materials.

phrases.english: and bring them in over there.
phrases.notes: Into the new shul.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא הֲוָה קָא בָנֵי בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about tearing down a shul to build another.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the old shul's materials would be used directly for a new shul.

steps.title: Does רב חסדא's rule apply when the old shul feeds the new one?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא recalled רב חסדא's rule: do not tear down a shul until another is built. That rule exists because of a worry about פשיעותא (people neglecting to rebuild). He asked whether it still applies when the old shul's own materials are needed for the new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sat and wondered about that ruling of רב חסדא, for רב חסדא said: One should not demolish a synagogue until one builds another synagogue. There, it is because of negligence. In a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר אבא asks whether the reason behind רב חסדא's rule fits his case. If the reason does not fit, maybe the rule does not apply either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's worry is that once the shul is torn down, people may never build a new one, and the town is left with no shul. Here the demolition is itself part of building the new shul. So the worry seems smaller, and the question is whether the rule still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: he was in doubt / he wondered
in a case like this, what (is the law)?

steps.confusionAlert: רמי בר אבא does not reject רב חסדא's rule. He accepts it and only asks whether it covers his special case.

phrases.english: He sat and was in doubt about
that (ruling) of Rav Chisda,
for Rav Chisda said:
One should not demolish a synagogue
until one builds another synagogue —
there it is because of negligence,
phrases.notes: The reason behind the rule.

phrases.english: in a case like this, what (is the law)?
phrases.notes: When the old materials go straight into the new shul.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב וְקָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ הָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the legal doubt that the case in step 4 creates.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב חסדא's ban apply when the demolition is needed to build the new shul, so the worry about negligence seems absent?

steps.title: רב פפא and רב הונא both forbid it
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא asked רב פפא, who forbade it. He then asked רב הונא, who also forbade it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב פפא, and he forbade him. Before רב הונא, and he forbade him.
steps.whatsHappening: Two rabbis answer the question from step 5. Both say no: even in this case, do not tear down the old shul first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the materials are meant for the new shul, the rule still applies. Building plans can stall, and the town could end up with no shul at all. So רב חסדא's rule holds even here.
steps.whatToRemember: One may not tear down an existing shul before a new one is built. This holds even if the old shul's materials are needed for the new one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא וַאֲסַר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He came before Rav Pappa, and he forbade him.
(He came) before Rav Huna, and he forbade him.
phrases.notes: A second, matching answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא וַאֲסַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר אבא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Forbidden. רב חסדא's rule applies even when the old shul's materials are meant for the new one.

steps.title: רבא: exchanging or selling a shul is allowed, renting or mortgaging is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a בית כנסת may be exchanged for another building or sold. It may not be rented out or mortgaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This synagogue, exchanging it or selling it is permitted; renting it out or mortgaging it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule that sorts which transactions with a shul building are allowed and which are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exchanging and selling are both permanent transfers. Renting and mortgaging are temporary uses, and the building is still owned as a shul. Step 8 explains why this difference matters.

phrases.english: Rava said:
This synagogue,
exchanging it or selling it is permitted,
phrases.notes: Permanent transfers.

phrases.english: renting it or mortgaging it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Temporary uses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא הַאי בֵּי כְנִישְׁתָּא חַלּוֹפַהּ וְזַבּוֹנַהּ שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by רבא about which transactions are allowed with a shul building.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exchanging or selling a shul is permitted. Renting or mortgaging it is forbidden.

steps.title: The reason: a rented shul stays holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבא's rule. A shul that is rented or mortgaged remains in its holy status, so using it for ordinary purposes is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It remains in its holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's rule and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sale or exchange moves the קדושה onto the money or the new building, so the old building becomes ordinary. Renting or mortgaging moves nothing, so the building is still holy. Letting a renter use it for ordinary things would be a misuse of a holy place.
steps.whatToRemember: A sale or exchange moves the shul's קדושה elsewhere. Renting or mortgaging leaves the building holy, so it is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think renting is lighter than selling and so should be easier to allow. It is the reverse: because renting is temporary, the holiness stays on the building, and that is why renting is forbidden.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: The גמרא asks and answers its own question.

phrases.english: It remains in its holiness.
phrases.notes: When rented or mortgaged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רבא's rule in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rented or mortgaged shul stays holy, so ordinary use of it is forbidden. A sale or exchange moves the holiness away from the building.

steps.title: The same rule applies to a shul's bricks
steps.stepSummary: The bricks of a בית כנסת follow רבא's rule. They may be exchanged or sold, but they may not be lent or rented out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bricks too: exchanging them or selling them is allowed, but renting them out is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes רבא's rule about the whole shul building and applies it to the shul's bricks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When bricks are sold or exchanged, their holiness moves onto the money or the item received, so they become ordinary. When they are rented out, the owner still has them and they stay holy, so using them for ordinary purposes is forbidden. This is the same reasoning the גמרא gave in step 8.

phrases.english: Bricks too (have the same rule):
phrases.notes: Refers to the bricks of a shul.

phrases.english: exchanging them and selling them is permitted,
renting them out is forbidden.
phrases.notes: The bricks stay holy while they are rented out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's rule from the shul building to its bricks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bricks of a shul may be exchanged or sold, but they may not be rented out.

steps.title: The rule applies only to old bricks, not new ones
steps.stepSummary: The ban on renting applies only to old bricks that were already part of a shul. New bricks that were only set aside for a shul may be rented out.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies to old bricks, but with new bricks we have no problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the brick rule. It covers only bricks that were actually used in a shul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holiness comes from real use in a shul. New bricks that were bought or set aside but never built into a shul have not become holy, so renting them is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Old ones (already used in the shul)
New ones (only set aside, never used)
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: These words apply to old (bricks),
but with new ones, we have no problem with it.
phrases.notes: New bricks were designated for the shul but never built into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the brick rule from step 9 to old bricks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only bricks that were actually used in a shul are holy. New bricks that were only set aside may be rented out.

steps.title: Why setting new bricks aside does not make them holy
steps.stepSummary: Even the view that הזמנה (designation) matters applies only when an object is made for its purpose, like weaving a garment for a dead person. Bricks that already existed and were later set aside are like spun thread later set aside for weaving, and on that case everyone agrees designation does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who says designation counts, that is only in a case like someone who weaves a garment for a dead person. But here, it is like spun thread set aside for weaving, and no one says designation counts there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question the learner would naturally ask: since the new bricks were set aside for a shul, shouldn't that make them holy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known view that הזמנה מילתא היא, meaning designation alone has legal effect. That view covers only an object made from the start for its purpose, like a shroud woven for a dead person. The bricks already existed and were only later set aside, like thread that was already spun. For that kind of case, nobody holds that designation has any effect.

keyTerms.meaning: One who weaves a garment for a dead person
There is no one who says so

steps.confusionAlert: This does not reject the view that הזמנה matters. It only shows that this case falls outside that view, because the bricks were not made for the shul. They were merely set aside for it afterward.

phrases.english: And even according to the one who says
that designation is significant,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי כְּגוֹן הָאוֹרֵג בֶּגֶד לַמֵּת.
phrases.english: that applies to a case like one who weaves a garment for a dead person.
phrases.notes: Here the object was made from the start for its purpose.

phrases.english: But here, it is like spun thread (set aside) for weaving,
phrases.notes: The material already existed before it was set aside.

phrases.english: and there is no one who says (designation counts there).

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הַזְמָנָה מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 10 against the possible claim that designation makes the new bricks holy.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Setting the new bricks aside for a shul should make them holy, according to the view that הזמנה מילתא היא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Designation counts only for an object made for its purpose. Bricks that already existed and were later set aside are not affected by designation, according to everyone.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about giving a shul as a gift
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue whether a shul may be given away as a מתנה. One forbids it and one permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gift: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about it. One forbids it and one permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a new case, a gift, which is in between a sale (allowed) and renting (forbidden). It presents a dispute, and the next two steps explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift is like a sale because ownership fully moves to someone else. But no money changes hands, so there is nothing for the holiness to move onto. That is why it is unclear which category a gift belongs to.

phrases.aramaic: מַתָּנָה, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא,
phrases.english: A gift: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it,
one forbids, and one permits.
phrases.notes: The גמרא does not say which of them holds which view.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתָּנָה, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bricks to a new kind of transfer: giving the shul as a gift.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute whether a shul may be given as a gift and then used for ordinary purposes.

steps.title: Reason for forbidding a gift
steps.stepSummary: The one who forbids asks how the holiness could leave the building, since nothing was received in return for the holiness to move onto.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids says: through what would its holiness be removed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the side that forbids giving a shul as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a sale, the holiness moves onto the money paid. In a gift, nothing comes back to the giver, so the holiness has nowhere to go. Therefore the shul stays holy.

phrases.english: The one who forbids (says):
Through what would its holiness be removed?!
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. There is nothing for the holiness to move onto.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the forbidding view in the dispute from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A gift brings nothing in return to absorb the holiness, so the shul stays holy.

steps.title: Reason for permitting a gift: a gift is like a sale
steps.stepSummary: The one who permits argues that no one gives a gift unless he gets some benefit from it. That benefit works like payment, so the gift is treated like a sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who permits says: if he did not get some benefit from it, he would not have given it. So the gift becomes like a sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the side that permits giving a shul as a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every giver gets something in return, such as goodwill or gratitude. That benefit plays the role of payment, so the holiness moves onto it, just as it moves onto money in a sale.
steps.whatToRemember: A sale is allowed because the holiness moves onto the payment. Renting is forbidden because the shul stays holy. A gift depends on whether the giver's benefit counts as payment.

phrases.english: And the one who permits (says):

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵּיהּ —
phrases.english: if he did not have benefit from him,
he would not have given it to him,
so the gift turns out to be like a sale.
phrases.notes: The giver's benefit works like payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּשָׁרֵי: אִי לָאו דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning to step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The giver's benefit acts like payment, so a gift is treated like a sale and the holiness moves onto that benefit.

steps.title: ברייתא‎: מצוה objects may be thrown out, holy objects must be buried
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that תשמישי מצוה may be thrown away after use, while תשמישי קדושה must be put away respectfully through burial (גניזה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: items used for a מצוה may be thrown out. Items used for holiness must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ברייתא that sorts holy objects into two groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing a מצוה with an object does not make the object holy, so it may be thrown out once it is no longer used. An object that serves something holy, like a Torah or anything with ה׳'s name, gains holiness itself and must be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this introduces a ברייתא)
Objects used to do a מצוה
Must be buried or stored away respectfully

steps.whyThisMatters: This split is a basic rule for how to dispose of old religious items in practice.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Articles of a מצוה may be thrown out.
Articles of holiness must be buried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section about how to dispose of holy objects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשמישי מצוה may be thrown out, but תשמישי קדושה must be buried.

steps.title: Which items belong to each group
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the items in each group. סוכה, לולב, שופר, and ציצית are תשמישי מצוה. Cases for scrolls, תפילין, מזוזות, a Torah case, a תפילין cover, and their straps are תשמישי קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are מצוה items: סוכה, לולב, שופר, ציצית. These are holy items: cases for scrolls, תפילין and מזוזות, a case for a ספר תורה, and a cover for תפילין and their straps.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues by giving examples so we know which objects fall into each group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items in the first group are used to do a מצוה but have no holy writing on them. The items in the second group either contain ה׳'s name, like תפילין and מזוזות, or directly hold something that does, like a Torah case.

keyTerms.meaning: A case for a Torah scroll
A cover or bag for תפילין

steps.whatToRemember: The test is simple. An object used for a מצוה may be thrown out. An object that holds or serves holy writing must be buried.

phrases.english: And these are articles of a מצוה:
a sukkah, a lulav, a shofar, tzitzis.
And these are articles of holiness:
cases of (holy) scrolls, tefillin and mezuzos,
and a case for a Torah scroll,
and a cover for tefillin, and their straps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the examples for the two groups set up in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סוכה, לולב, שופר, and ציצית are תשמישי מצוה. Scroll cases, תפילין, מזוזות, a Torah case, a תפילין cover, and straps are תשמישי קדושה.

steps.title: רבא changes his mind about the reading stand
steps.stepSummary: רבא first thought the כורסיא was only a תשמיש דתשמיש, which may be thrown away. After seeing a ספר תורה placed directly on it, he ruled that it is a תשמיש קדושה and may not be thrown away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: At first I used to say that this reading stand only serves something that serves the holy item, so it is permitted to throw it away. But once I saw that people sometimes place a ספר תורה directly on it, I said it directly serves holiness, and it is forbidden to throw it away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tells us he changed his ruling about the reading stand in shul. The change came from what he saw people actually doing with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a cloth sits between the ספר תורה and the stand, so the stand only serves the cloth. That makes it a lower level, a תשמיש דתשמיש. Once the ספר תורה rests directly on the stand, the stand serves the holy object itself and moves up to תשמיש קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: The reading stand (lectern) on which the Torah is read
Something that serves an item that serves holiness (a second-level item)
At first I used to say

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different levels here. A תשמיש דתשמיש is one step removed from the holy object and may be thrown away. A תשמיש קדושה touches or serves the holy object directly and needs גניזה. The whole question is which level the stand belongs to.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the test for the rest of this passage: an object's status depends on how it is actually used with the holy object.

phrases.english: Rava said: At first I used to say:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי כּוּרְסְיָא, תַּשְׁמִישׁ דְּתַשְׁמִישׁ הוּא, וּשְׁרֵי.
phrases.english: This reading stand is an item that serves something that serves holiness, and it is permitted (to discard).
phrases.notes: Normally a cloth separates the stand from the Torah scroll.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזֵינָא דְּמוֹתְבִי עִלָּוֵיהּ סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Once I saw that they place a Torah scroll directly on it,
I said: It is an item that serves holiness, and it is forbidden (to discard).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא's categories (תשמישי מצוה versus תשמישי קדושה) to a new object, the reading stand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כורסיא is a תשמיש קדושה, because a ספר תורה is sometimes placed directly on it. It may not be thrown away.

steps.title: רבא changes his mind about the ark curtain
steps.stepSummary: In the same way, רבא first thought the ark curtain was only a תשמיש דתשמיש. After seeing it folded and used as a resting place for a ספר תורה, he ruled that it is a תשמיש קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא also said: At first I used to say that this curtain only serves something that serves holiness. But once I saw that people fold it and set a Torah scroll on it, I said it directly serves holiness, and it is forbidden to throw it away.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second ruling built the same way as the first, this time about the curtain hanging in front of the ark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curtain normally just decorates the ark, so it serves the ark and not the scroll. Once people fold it and rest the scroll on it, it serves the scroll directly. It therefore moves up to תשמיש קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain hung in front of the ark (פָּרוֹכֶת)

phrases.english: And Rava said: At first I used to say:
This curtain is an item that serves something that serves holiness.
phrases.notes: It decorates the ark rather than serving the scroll itself.

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזֵינָא דְּעָיְיפִי לֵיהּ וּמַנְּחִי סִיפְרָא עִלָּוֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Once I saw that they fold it over and place the scroll on it,
I said: It is an item that serves holiness, and it is forbidden (to discard).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling using the same reasoning as Step 17, applied to a different object.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ark curtain is a תשמיש קדושה, because a ספר תורה is sometimes placed on it. It may not be thrown away.

steps.title: Reusing a broken ark
steps.stepSummary: The wood of a broken תיבה may be made into a smaller תיבה. It may not be made into a כורסיא, which is a less holy item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: An ark that has fallen apart may be made into a smaller ark. That is permitted. Making it into a reading stand is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves to a new question: what may be done with the materials of a holy item once it breaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A smaller ark has the same level of holiness as the original ark, so reusing the materials that way is fine. A reading stand is a lower level than the ark. Taking holy materials down to a lower level is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The ark in which the Torah scroll is kept

phrases.english: And Rava said: This ark that fell apart,
to make it into a small ark is permitted,
phrases.notes: Same level of holiness.

phrases.english: (but to make it into) a reading stand is forbidden.
phrases.notes: A lower level of holiness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the status of objects to the rules for reusing broken holy objects. It also relies on Step 17's point that the reading stand is a holy item, though a lower one than the ark.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Materials from a broken ark may be reused for something equally holy, like a smaller ark. They may not be used for something less holy, like a reading stand.

steps.title: Reusing a worn-out ark curtain
steps.stepSummary: A worn-out ark curtain may be made into a wrapping cloth for a full ספר תורה. It may not be made into a wrapping for a חומש, which is less holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A curtain that has worn out may be made into a wrapping cloth for Torah scrolls. That is permitted. Making it into a wrapping for single books of the Torah is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second reuse ruling that works the same way as the broken-ark ruling, this time for a worn curtain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wrapping that touches a full ספר תורה serves something at least as holy as what the curtain served, so reusing the curtain that way is allowed. A חומש, a scroll of just one of the five books, has a lower holiness than a full ספר תורה. Using the curtain for a חומש would take it down a level.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrolls of a single book of the Torah (a חומש)

steps.confusionAlert: Here ספרי means full Torah scrolls, not just any books. The contrast is between a complete ספר תורה, which is holier, and a single-book חומש, which is less holy.

phrases.english: And Rava said: This curtain that wore out,
to make it into a wrapping cloth for Torah scrolls is permitted,
(but making it into a wrapping) for single-book scrolls is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel to Step 19 that applies the same reuse principle to cloth instead of wood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worn curtain may become a wrapping for a full ספר תורה, but not a wrapping for a חומש.
steps.whatToRemember: The reuse rule: holy materials may be reused at the same level of holiness or a higher one, but never at a lower one.

steps.title: Storage cases and sacks for scrolls require burial
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that cases for חומשים and sacks for ספרי תורה are תשמישי קדושה and must be buried in גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These cases for single-book scrolls and sacks for Torah scrolls count as items that serve holiness, and they must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives one more status ruling, about the bags and cases that scrolls are stored in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These containers hold the holy scrolls directly, so רבא puts them in the category of תשמיש קדושה. That means they cannot simply be thrown out when they are no longer used. They must be put away respectfully through burial.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacks or bags used for storage
They are put away by burial

phrases.english: And Rava said: These cases for single-book scrolls
and sacks for Torah scrolls,
they are items that serve holiness, and they are buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי זְבִילֵי דְחוּמָּשֵׁי וְקַמְטְרֵי דְסִפְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to defining the status of objects, much like the cases in the ברייתא of Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cases and sacks for scrolls are תשמישי קדושה and require גניזה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's last ruling as too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to teach this at all. This question sets up the next step, which explains what the ruling adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 16 already listed cases for scrolls as תשמישי קדושה. Containers that hold scrolls directly seem clearly to belong there. So the גמרא asks what new information רבא is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a ruling adds nothing new)

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether Step 21 is needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that cases and sacks for scrolls are תשמישי קדושה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Containers that hold scrolls directly obviously serve holiness, and the ברייתא already lists cases for scrolls. The ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Items made for protection still count as holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have thought storage containers, made only to protect the scrolls and not to honor them, are not תשמישי קדושה. רבא teaches that they still are.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that these items are not made for honor, only for protection, so they do not count. Therefore רבא teaches us that they do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge by showing the mistake רבא's ruling prevents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wrappings and stands are used to honor the scroll. Storage sacks and cases are mostly practical, made to keep the scroll safe. One might think that purely practical items do not get holy status. רבא teaches that serving the scroll for protection is enough to make them תשמישי קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken view the ruling prevents)
He teaches us (this is the new information)

steps.whatToRemember: An item that directly serves a holy scroll is a תשמיש קדושה even if it was made only to protect the scroll and not to honor it.

phrases.english: You might have said:
These are not made for honor,
they are made merely for protection,
so he teaches us (that they are still items that serve holiness).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the ruling prevents a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Items made only to protect the scrolls, and not to honor them, might not count as תשמישי קדושה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even protective containers that serve holy scrolls are תשמישי קדושה and require גניזה.

steps.title: Priests want to pray in a synagogue next to a room with a dead body
steps.stepSummary: A synagogue in רומי opened into a room where a dead body lay. The כהנים wanted to enter to pray, so they asked רבא what to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a synagogue of the Jews of Rome that opened into a room where a dead body was lying. The priests wanted to go in and pray there. They came and asked רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story and sets up a practical problem. רבא will answer it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead body spreads טומאת אוהל through an open doorway into the connected room. A כהן may not become טמא from a מת, so the כהנים could not enter the synagogue unless something blocked the opening.

keyTerms.meaning: כהנים, who may not become טמא from a dead body
Ritual impurity that comes from a corpse

phrases.english: There was a certain synagogue
of the (Jews of) Rome
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'of the Jews' here; the corrected wording leaves out the words in round brackets and adds the letter in square brackets, so it reads 'of Rome.'

phrases.english: that was open to a certain room
in which a dead body was lying,
and the priests wanted
to go in to pray there.
They came and told it to רבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story begins: a practical problem about טומאת מת in a synagogue, which רבא will try to solve using the synagogue ark.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can כהנים enter a synagogue that is connected by an open doorway to a room containing a dead body?

steps.title: רבא says to use the ark as a barrier in the doorway
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells them to lift the ark and set it down in the opening. A wooden vessel made to stay in one place cannot become טמא, so it blocks the טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Lift the ark and set it down in the doorway. It is a wooden vessel made to rest in one place. A wooden vessel made to rest does not receive טומאה, and it blocks the טומאה from passing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the כהנים' question. He uses the ark itself to seal off the doorway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only an object that cannot itself become טמא can act as a barrier against טומאה. A wooden vessel that is made to stay put, and not to be carried around, is not מקבל טומאה. So the ark can block the doorway.

keyTerms.meaning: The ark (תיבה) that holds the ספר תורה
A wooden vessel made to stay at rest in one place

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a wooden vessel can never become טמא. Most wooden vessels can. Only one made to stay in one place is excluded, and that is the key to רבא's answer.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Lift up the ark and set it down (in the opening),

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ כְּלִי עֵץ הֶעָשׂוּי לְנַחַת,
phrases.english: since it is a wooden vessel made to rest in place,
and a wooden vessel made to rest in place
does not receive ritual impurity
and it blocks the impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step answers the question raised in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Place the ark in the doorway. As a wooden vessel made to rest in place, it cannot become טמא, so it blocks the טומאה.

steps.title: The רבנן object that the ark is sometimes carried with a ספר תורה inside
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן point out that the ark is sometimes moved while a ספר תורה is still inside it. That makes it a vessel carried both full and empty, which can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבא: But sometimes they move it while a ספר תורה is resting in it. So it is a vessel that is carried both full and empty!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רבא's answer. They attack the claim that the ark is a vessel made to rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wooden vessel that is carried around even when it is full is treated like a normal vessel, and it can become טמא. If the ark is sometimes moved with a ספר תורה inside, it is not a vessel made to rest. Then it cannot serve as a barrier.

keyTerms.meaning: Moved around both when full and when empty, which makes a wooden vessel able to become טמא

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to רבא:
But sometimes they move it
while a Torah scroll is resting in it,
so it is a vessel moved both full and empty!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: וְהָא זִמְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step challenges רבא's ruling in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the ark is a כלי עץ העשוי לנחת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In practice the ark is sometimes carried with a ספר תורה inside. That makes it a vessel that is moved full and empty, so it can become טמא and cannot block טומאה.

steps.title: רבא accepts the objection and says there is no solution
steps.stepSummary: רבא admits that if so, his solution does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts the רבנן's challenge. The suggested fix is dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not defend his idea. Since the ark is sometimes carried while full, it can become טמא and cannot serve as a barrier. The story ends with no solution for the כהנים.
steps.whatToRemember: An object can block טומאה only if it cannot become טמא itself. The synagogue ark fails this test because it is sometimes carried with a ספר תורה inside.

phrases.english: If so, it is not possible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא concedes to the objection in step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ark cannot be used as a barrier against טומאה, so the problem in the synagogue has no remedy.

steps.title: Worn-out Torah wrappings become shrouds for an abandoned body
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rules that worn-out wrapping cloths of ספרים may be made into burial shrouds for a מת מצוה. This counts as their proper burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: Wrapping cloths of ספרים that have worn out may be made into shrouds for a מת מצוה, and this is their burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of what to do with worn-out holy items. מר זוטרא gives a new ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a worn-out תשמיש קדושה must be buried. Here, using the cloths to wrap a מת מצוה, a body with no one else to bury it, is itself treated as a respectful burial. This counts as their גניזה, not as a downgrade to a less holy use.

keyTerms.meaning: Cloths used to wrap holy scrolls
An unattended dead body with no one else to bury it
Respectful burial or storage of holy items

phrases.english: מר זוטרא said:
Wrapping cloths of scrolls that wore out —
we make them into shrouds
for a מת מצוה,
and this is their burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: מִטְפְּחוֹת סְפָרִים שֶׁבָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step returns to the theme of steps 20 and 21: how worn-out תשמישי קדושה are treated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Worn-out scroll wrappings may be used as shrouds for a מת מצוה, and this fulfills their requirement of גניזה.

steps.title: A worn-out ספר תורה is buried next to a תלמיד חכם
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a worn-out ספר תורה is buried next to a תלמיד חכם, even one who only learns basic הלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A ספר תורה that wore out is buried next to a תלמיד חכם, and even next to one who only studies הלכות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another ruling about burying holy items, this time the ספר תורה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burying a worn-out ספר תורה next to someone who learned Torah honors it. The words 'even one who only studies הלכות' widen the definition of תלמיד חכם to include someone who knows the material without deep analysis.

keyTerms.meaning: We bury or put away respectfully
One who learns and reviews הלכות without deep analysis

phrases.english: And רבא said:
A Torah scroll that wore out —
we bury it next to a Torah scholar,
and even one who only studies הלכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step adds another burial rule, for the ספר תורה itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worn-out ספר תורה is buried next to a תלמיד חכם, which includes even a שונה הלכות.

steps.title: The buried Torah scroll is placed in a clay vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב adds that the worn-out ספר תורה is buried inside a clay vessel. He supports this from a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: And it is placed in a clay vessel, as it says: 'And put them in an earthenware vessel, so that they may last many days.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב adds a detail to רבא's ruling and brings a פסוק as a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the scroll in a clay jar protects it from decaying quickly. The פסוק in ירמיהו shows that a clay vessel is used to preserve documents 'for many days.' This adds honor and protection to the burial.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is stated (introduces a פסוק)
Many days, meaning a long time

steps.whatToRemember: Worn-out holy items are buried with respect. Wrappings may become shrouds for a מת מצוה, and a ספר תורה is buried next to a תלמיד חכם inside a clay jar.

phrases.english: רב אחא בר יעקב said:
And in a clay vessel,
as it is stated:
"And put them in an earthenware vessel
so that they may last many days."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: וּבִכְלִי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step adds a detail to רבא's ruling in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The worn-out ספר תורה is buried in a כלי חרס, based on ירמיהו 32:14.

steps.title: A בית כנסת may become a בית מדרש, but not the reverse
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, quoting רבא, rules that a בית כנסת may be turned into a בית מדרש, but a בית מדרש may not be turned into a בית כנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: changing a synagogue into a study hall is permitted. Changing a study hall into a synagogue is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבא about turning one kind of holy building into another. Going from בית כנסת to בית מדרש is allowed, and going the other way is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling follows the rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין: you may only raise something in holiness, never lower it. Since a בית כנסת may become a בית מדרש, the בית מדרש must be the holier of the two. Turning a בית מדרש back into a בית כנסת would be a step down, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Synagogue (בית כנסת), a building for prayer
Study hall (בית מדרש), a building for Torah learning

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא ranks holy places by their level of קדושה. That ranking decides which changes to a building are allowed.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
phrases.notes: This just tells us who said the ruling that comes next.

phrases.english: From a synagogue to a study hall: permitted,
phrases.notes: Going up in holiness is allowed.

phrases.english: from a study hall to a synagogue: forbidden.
phrases.notes: Going down in holiness is not allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from burying worn-out holy objects (steps 28-30) to a new question: changing the use of holy buildings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית כנסת may be converted into a בית מדרש, but a בית מדרש may not be converted into a בית כנסת, because the בית מדרש is holier.

steps.title: Another version of רבא's ruling teaches the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא quotes רבא with the reverse ruling: a בית מדרש may become a בית כנסת, but not the other way. Then רב אחא begins a statement that continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא, quoting רבא, teaches it the opposite way. רב אחא said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records a second, opposite tradition of what רבא said. It then sets up the next move by introducing a statement from רב אחא, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא's version, the בית כנסת is the holier building. So changing a בית מדרש into a בית כנסת is the upgrade, and the reverse is forbidden. The two students disagree about what their teacher רבא said, not about the rule מעלין בקודש ולא מורידין itself.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise in holiness and do not lower: the principle behind both versions

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפי (פ-פ-י) and רב פפא (פ-פ-א) are two different אמוראים with very similar names. Here they report opposite versions of the same teaching of רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רבא's ruling. רב פפי says the בית מדרש is holier, and רב פפא says the בית כנסת is holier. רב אחא's statement on the next amud will weigh in.

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa, in the name of Rava,
phrases.notes: A different student of רבא with a different tradition.

phrases.english: teaches the opposite.
phrases.notes: Study hall to synagogue is permitted; synagogue to study hall is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Acha said:
phrases.notes: This introduces what רב אחא said, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנִי אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of the same ruling of רבא quoted in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב פפא's version, a בית מדרש may be converted into a בית כנסת but not the reverse, because the בית כנסת is holier.
